The *Takkapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 63), rendered in English as *The Buttermilk Sage*, is a canonical story from the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. Set at the Jetavana monastery, the narrative frame concerns a monk overcome by sensual desire. Addressing the monk, the Buddha declares that women are treacherous and ungrateful, and relates a story of the past to dispel his infatuation [SuttaCentral].
